note: Form-resistant questions pulled from packs during the 3b content pass. Not shipped, not deleted — awaiting a "pick all that are correct" multi-select form. See Docs/CONTENT-PASS-PLAN.md.

question.ask: Name the four countries that make up the United Kingdom.
question.answer: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland

questions.subject: geography
questions.reason: Resists mcq: the answer is a set of four items, not one option, so no single-item distractor set is honest. Resists truefalse: a slotted claim would only test one country's membership at a time, which is a different (and lesser) fact than naming all four. This is the canonical example from CONTENT-RULES.md — genuinely a set-answer question, a fit for a future multi-select form.

question.ask: Why is friction useful when you are walking?
question.answer: It stops your feet slipping and helps you grip the ground

questions.subject: science
questions.reason: Resists mcq: the answer is an explanation (grip + prevents slipping), not a single fact with unambiguously wrong alternatives. Resists truefalse: any slotted claim would test a narrower fact (e.g. 'friction helps you grip') and lose the explanatory 'why'. This is the second canonical example named in CONTENT-RULES.md/DRAFTER-INSTRUCTIONS.md.

question.ask: Why does a shadow have roughly the same shape as the object that makes it?
question.answer: Because the object blocks the light in that shape
acceptableAnswers: the object blocks the light in its shape
the light is blocked in the shape of the object

questions.subject: science
questions.reason: Resists mcq and truefalse: the answer is a causal explanation of why shadows take the shape they do, not a single named fact. A slotted claim would flatten the 'why' into a narrower, less useful statement.

question.ask: Why do cyclists wear reflective strips at night?
question.answer: so light from car headlights bounces back and drivers can see them

questions.subject: science
questions.reason: Resists open: the answer is a multi-part causal explanation (headlight light reflects off the strip, so drivers notice the cyclist), too long to stand as a short canonical answer. Resists truefalse: a slotted claim would flatten the 'why' into a narrower fact and lose the causal chain. Only a working mcq exists, and per the 'complete or quarantine' rule a partial-forms question does not stay in the corpus.

question.ask: Put these stages in the correct order.
question.answer: pollination → seed formation → seed dispersal → new plant grows
distractors: seed dispersal → pollination → new plant grows → seed formation
new plant grows → pollination → seed dispersal → seed formation

questions.subject: science
questions.reason: Resists open: the answer is a four-item ordered sequence, not a short single fact. Resists truefalse: a slotted claim can only swap one item at a time, which tests a much narrower (and less useful) fact than the whole ordering. This is a sequencing question — a strong fit for a future ordering/multi-select form, not the current three.

question.ask: Why is it useful for seeds to be spread far away from the parent plant?
question.answer: So the new plants have space, light and water and do not have to compete with the parent plant
acceptableAnswers: so they have room to grow
so they don't compete for light and water

questions.subject: science
questions.reason: Resists mcq and truefalse: the answer is a causal explanation (avoiding competition for space, light and water), not a single named fact with unambiguously wrong alternatives.

question.ask: Which order is correct for how a butterfly grows?

questions.subject: science
questions.reason: Resists open and truefalse for the same reason as the plants pack's life-cycle ordering question (lc-3): the answer is a four-item sequence, not a short single fact or a claim that a single {} slot can carry.
